answer: A limited-vouching graph throttles sybils at the door: a new agent can join only when an established agent spends one of its few vouching slots, and the voucher's own standing is slashed if the newcomer is proven a duplicate. Like a summit pass checked at a single narrow trail, entry cannot be mass-produced, and the horizon of trust stays visible because every vouch is public. A farmer who wants a thousand clones must first capture or bribe many trusted vouchers, each risking its own reputation, while a karst landscape of hidden shortcuts offers no bypass around the gate.
